builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
summary: Replaces DPO-based prompt-injection defense training (e.g., Meta-SecAlign) with the SecPO loss anchored on an approximated injection-invariant reference model plus an adversarial training pipeline that synthesizes strong best@240 injections. Costs are a full adversarial fine-tuning run with attack synthesis (240-step optimization per sample) on a 27B model, which likely exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without third-party training APIs, though the released model and training data are freely usable. Can fail against novel adaptive attacks outside the training distribution, and reported gains are validated mainly on the authors' attack suite and AgentDojo benchmark.
rationale: Prompt injection is a top production threat for tool-using agents, and the released defended model and data allow low-cost evaluation, but reproducing the full training pipeline locally is infeasible on 24 GB so the reader should test the released checkpoint rather than retrain.
technique: SecPO adversarial training for prompt injection defense

claims.statement: Replaces DPO-based prompt-injection defense training (e.g., Meta-SecAlign) with the SecPO loss anchored on an approximated injection-invariant reference model plus an adversarial training pipeline that synthesizes strong best@240 injections. Costs are a full adversarial fine-tuning run with attack synthesis (240-step optimization per sample) on a 27B model, which likely exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without third-party training APIs, though the released model and training data are freely usable. Can fail against novel adaptive attacks outside the training distribution, and reported gains are validated mainly on the authors' attack suite and AgentDojo benchmark.

SecPO loss reduces attack success rates by a further 2.4-4.6x compared with DPO loss on top of adversarial training; SecPO+AT Qwen3.6-27B reaches 8.8% vs 78.8% AgentDojo ASR@800 vs Meta-SecAlign, with no noticeable utility loss across nine benchmarks.
